title: Cinéma Vérité
description: Cinéma vérité uses available light, zoom-to-find framing, and the filmmaker's presence as a catalyst, so the camera is admitted into the room rather than hidden. Unpretty 16mm or digital frames, mixed color temperature, and a zoom hunting the moment are the physical signature, not a recovered amateur tape.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Life is not staged for a key light. Someone talks, the zoom finds them, a window or a practical is the source, and the filmmaker's question or proximity changes what happens.
The frame can be late, centered wrong, or blown at the window. That is the contract.
It is the wrong tool when polish is the point, or when a fictional camcorder is the story. Blockbuster Gloss would be propaganda here.
Found footage needs a diegetic operator in danger. Documentary is broader: interviews, archive, and observation that may sit back.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Available light only, or a small on-camera bounce that still reads as room light. 16mm or a long ENG zoom (the 12-120 class), hunting focus and size.
Handheld or a monopod, eye height, reacting. Leave mixed tungsten and daylight.
Do not add a rim or a pretty backlight. Prompt available light, unpretty frames, zooming to find, life unstaged.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when style would feel like a lie and the filmmaker's presence is part of the event. Do not use it as a shake filter on a scripted scene that still has three-point lighting.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Cinéma vérité is intervention and available light in documentary reality. Documentary includes sit-down interviews and archive.
French New Wave borrows the tools for fiction, then adds jump cuts and cinephile blocking. Handheld is only the body.
Available Light is only the source. Found Footage invents a tape inside the story.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Found Footage or pretty Documentary: a timestamp and panic, or a keyed interview with a clean backlight. The tell is three-point light, a rim, or a device story.
Fix: kill the film lights, let the zoom hunt, and keep the filmmaker in the room as a presence, not a horror operator.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Cinéma Vérité in film?
A documentary look in which available light, zoom-to-find framing, and the filmmaker's presence provoke or witness unstaged life. The camera is a catalyst, not a hidden observer with a key and a rim.
Cinéma Vérité vs Documentary

Documentary is a broad rhetoric: interview, archive, observation, even mock forms. Cinéma vérité is a specific physical method: available light, zoom, presence. A sit-down with a window key can be documentary without being vérité.
When should I use Cinéma Vérité?

When prettifying the room would feel like propaganda, and the filmmaker's being there matters. Skip it for recovered-tape horror, for billboard gloss, or for a scripted scene that still wants a rim light.
How do I prompt Cinéma Vérité for AI image or video?
Write: Cinéma vérité treatment of [Subject], available light, unpretty frames, zooming to find, mixed color, life unstaged. Name the real source. Do not add a timestamp, a rim, or a crane.
